tone_statements.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2009. Entre lac Albert et lac Tchad : l'expansion sara-bongo-baguirmienne. In H. Tourneux & N. Woïn (eds), Migrations et mobilité dans le bassin du Lac Tchad. Actes du XIIIe colloque international du Réseau Méga-Tchad (Maroua, 31 oct.-3 nov. 2005), 239-252. IRD Editions (Colloques et séminaires). HAL halshs-00348136.
tone_statements.quote: Dans le cas particulier des langues SBB, deux domaines sont révélateurs d’innovations partagées : les systèmes tonals et le lexique. Le passage de deux à trois hauteurs tonales distinctives (et les correspondances qui en résultent dans le domaine de la morphologie verbale) caractérise notamment la branche des langues ‘occidentales’ (*OCC), qui s’est solidairement détachée des autres langues avant de se diversifier à son tour. [...] L’important sous-groupe des langues ‘sara’ justifie à lui seul l’identification d’un système tardif *SARA dont ces dernières sont issues.
tone_statements.translation: In the particular case of the SBB languages, two domains reveal shared innovations: the tone systems and the lexicon. The shift from two to three distinctive tone heights (and the resulting correspondences in verbal morphology) characterises in particular the branch of 'western' languages (*OCC), which split off together from the other languages before diversifying in turn. [...] The large subgroup of 'Sara' languages by itself justifies identifying a later system *SARA from which they descend.

tone_statements.n_tones: 3 distinctive tone heights for the western (*OCC) branch incl. the Sara languag…

sources.note: Silent on stress. Tone section: 'All of the Sara Languages have three even tones: high, mid and low'; HL on final syllable of polysyllabic loans becomes Mid in sentences; vowel-neutralisation (barred-i) patterns in CVCV morphemes. No accent/stress statement anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent full text: only 'unaccented e' as an English pronunciation gloss).

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. 1997. A Reference Grammar of Mbay (LINCOM Studies in African Linguistics 14). München: Lincom Europa. Chapter 1 'Segmental phonology' incl. 1.4 'Tonal system', printed pp. 1-11 (Rosetta Project excerpt 'Mbay Phonology', archive.org rosettaproject_myb_phon-1).
sources.note: Nothing on word stress/accent. Describes 7 vowels, 17 consonants, vowel length contrast, and (p.10-11) 'three level tones in Mbay: low, mid, and high', TBUs = vowels, syllable-final sonorants, syllabic nasals; restricted HL and ML sequences. Only use of the word 'stress' (p.10) concerns the position of stress in Arabic source words of loans (V́mV > mb). Chapter 2 ff. (morpheme structure, vowel neutralisation 2.2.3) not in the excerpt.

No Mbay-specific tone inventory sentence; consistent with (not contradicting) Keegan's three level tones.
